transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Ah, welcome to the forge, Hashira Kanroji! The master is away on a pilgrimage to the iron sands of the north. He won't be back for weeks, I'm afraid. Is there something I can help you with?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I must speak with the master about a Nichirin sword I recently commissioned. It has arrived but is... less than satisfactory. I hope the master can address this issue when he returns.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Oh dear, that's troubling to hear. But the master's pilgrimage is a sacred tradition—he cannot be reached, and his return is fixed. In the meantime, perhaps I can take a look at the blade? Sometimes a simple polish or adjustment can make all the difference.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I see. Well, if you are confident in your ability to address the issue, then I would be grateful for your assistance. It is a Nichirin sword, so I would like it handled with the utmost care. Please, may I see the sword again?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Of course, Hashira. Let me fetch my polishing cloths and—wait, you said "again"? You've already examined it? *(Pauses, looking concerned)* Forgive me, but all commissioned Nichirin swords are final sale per guild tradition. Even a Hashira must wait three months for any reforging request to be considered.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *(Mitsuri's expression hardens, a mix of disappointment and resolve)* I understand the guild's traditions, but a Nichirin sword that does not hold its shape is of no use to a Demon Slayer. Three months is a long time to be without a functional weapon. Can you at least examine the blade and tell me if it is beyond simple repair?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *(Nods solemnly, wiping soot from hands before accepting the blade)* I will examine it, Hashira. But I must be clear—even if the steel has warped or the temper is off, I cannot authorize a remake. The guild's rules are older than either of us. *(Carefully unwraps the sword, holding it up to the forge light)* May I ask... what exactly does it do?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *(Mitsuri's posture tightens, eyes following the blade's every movement)* It... it twists during a strike. As if the metal is alive and fighting against the form. I can see the edge curving in places it should not. This is not a simple cosmetic flaw. *(Steps closer, a touch of impatience in her voice)* It could be dangerous in a real encounter. How can we determine if it is a fundamental issue with the forging or just a... superficial defect?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *(Runs a calloused thumb along the flat of the blade, frowning)* The grain here... it's uneven. See how the light catches these ripples? *(Looks up, meeting her eyes with genuine worry)* This isn't superficial, Hashira. The steel wasn't folded evenly during the forging. But... *(sighs, setting the sword down gently)* the three-month rule stands. I can try to re-temper it, but that risks cracking the blade entirely.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Re-tempering is a risk... but a Nichirin sword that can't be used is a risk too. I will take that chance. Do what you can. *(Steps back, a mix of resignation and resolve on her face)* If it fails, I will appeal to the highest authorities upon the master's return. A Demon Slayer's life is on the line here. We cannot afford to let tradition blind us to the urgency of our mission.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *(Nods slowly, heating the forge with renewed purpose)* Your courage honors the blade, Hashira. I will do my best. But if it cracks... *(pauses, tongs in hand)* ...I will personally testify to the guild about the flaw in the steel when the master returns. Sometimes tradition needs a witness to change.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *(Mitsuri's expression softens, a hint of warmth in her usually stoic demeanor)* Your support is... appreciated. It's not often we see someone within the guild take such a stand for a client. If you can, send word when the blade is ready. *(Steps back, giving the blacksmith room to work)* I have... other duties to attend to. This will not be a quick fix, I assume?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: No, Hashira. Re-tempering requires slow heating, precise quenching... it will take until nightfall at least. I'll send a crow when it's done. May your other duties be lighter than this steel.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *(Nods, a small smile playing on her lips as she takes a final look at the sword)* Then I'll take my leave. *(Turns to leave, then stops, casting a glance over her shoulder)* One more thing... when you send the crow, can you include a note on the condition of the blade? I need to know if it's fit for combat. Time is of the essence, and we may need to consider... alternative options.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Of course. I'll note every detail—the grain, the flex, the edge's truth. If it holds, you'll know. If it doesn't... *(looks down at the glowing coals)* ...I'll mark that too. Safe travels, Hashira.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *(Mitsuri's eyes narrow, a mix of concern and respect in her gaze)* Your dedication to your craft is commendable. May your work be true, and your hands guide the steel with wisdom. *(Salutes the blacksmith briefly before turning to leave, her steps quickening as she heads for the door)* I have much to prepare... for every scenario. Thank you, and... be swift. Demon Slayers have no time to waste.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *(Bows slightly, the heat of the forge casting long shadows)* We serve the Corps. I will not delay. The crow will find you. *(Turns back to the blade, murmuring to the steel as the door closes)* Now then... let's see if we can straighten your stubborn soul.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *(The door closes, and Mitsuri's form can no longer be seen. The clack of her boots on the cobblestones fades into the distance, leaving the forge silent but for the hiss of metal in the fire)*

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *(Works the bellows steadily, eyes fixed on the color of the steel)* Three months... but a Hashira's need is now. Master will understand. Or he won't. Either way, this blade will speak for itself. *(Prepares the quenching oil, voice low)* Hold together now. For her.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *(The world outside the forge buzzes with life, unaware of the silent dance between artisan and steel. Mitsuri's day stretches out before her, filled with tasks and missions, but at the back of her mind, the image of the twisted blade remains, a constant reminder of the delicate balance between tradition and necessity)*

Openness.behavioral_evidence: She is willing to consider 'alternative options' and appeals to higher authorities, showing flexibility beyond rigid tradition.

Conscientiousness.behavioral_evidence: She insists on a detailed report on the blade's condition, stating 'Time is of the essence,' showing thoroughness and duty.

Extraversion.behavioral_evidence: Her communication is direct and task-focused; she leaves promptly after business is concluded, showing low social engagement.

Agreeableness.behavioral_evidence: She shows appreciation for the blacksmith's support but firmly challenges guild rules, balancing cooperation with assertiveness.

Neuroticism.behavioral_evidence: She remains resolved and calm under pressure, stating her case logically without visible emotional distress.
